status.label: Known numeric precision limitation
status.detail: Exact arbitrary-size integer arithmetic is not guaranteed by the current calculator engine/conversion path.

next_action.label: Decide numeric-precision scope
next_action.reason: A broader numeric model decision is needed rather than an unsupported one-line overflow fix.

judgment.rationale: The maintainer discussion identifies the Mages numeric representation as a known precision limitation. Inspected code evaluates with Mages and then converts to decimal; changing final display rounding cannot recover precision already lost.
evidence: The body gives exact expected and actual values for 2^64; a follow-up supplies 2^63-1.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/32014#issuecomment-2016160267 identifies the known Mages data-type limitation.
src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.Calculator/CalculateEngine.cs evaluates _magesEngine.Interpret, calls Convert.ToDecimal, and only then applies decimal-place rounding.
The linked issue timeline contains related precision reports but no targeted implementation.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep as a numeric-capability/product decision or external-engine limitation; do not advertise an exact-integer bug fix without an agreed numeric model.

fix_assessment.rationale: The requested exact-integer result exceeds the currently discussed engine capability. Replacing numeric semantics is a capability/dependency decision, not an established local rounding correction.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run Calculator loses low-order digits for large powers of two and near-Int64 values; the discussion identifies an existing numeric-engine precision limitation.
known_information: PowerToys 0.79.0, expression 2^64, and exact expected/actual output are supplied.
The follow-up shows an analogous error for 2^63-1.
A maintainer names Mages data types; available code has a Mages-to-decimal conversion before presentation.
inferences: The observed rounded-looking integer can involve engine/conversion precision; it must not simply be called arithmetic overflow from the screenshot.
issue_context.analysis: No additional reporter logs would establish arbitrary-precision engine support. Choosing exact-integer semantics is a maintainer product decision; the earlier handled-by-blank-assignee statement was false.
initial_investigation: Read the full body and all three comments, plus the linked precision-report timeline.
Inspected CalculateEngine evaluation/conversion/rounding and ResultHelper output formatting.
